chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

"Whoever comes to a barren, ruined land, extracts its water, irrigates its rivers, and develops it, then charity (khums/zakat) is upon him in it. If it was land belonging to a man before him, who was absent from it, left it, and ruined it, then later he came and claimed it, then the land belongs to Allah (Exalted and Mighty) and to the one who developed it."

key_terms.لِمَنْ عَمَرَهَا: To the one who developed it

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on owning and developing barren land when the original owner is absent?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates the principle of *Ihya al-Mawat* (reviving dead land), a cornerstone of Shia jurisprudence where cultivation confers ownership rights. It distinguishes between land with a present owner and *Mawat* (barren land left by an absent owner), establishing that the latter reverts to the cultivator as a manifestation of Allah’s grant. This ruling underscores the practical obligation of land development in Islamic governance and economic life.
